slides.texte_overlay:
unspoken rules of people
who seem effortlessly smart

they ask simple questions

they ask the obvious question everyone else was too proud to ask. being willing to look slow for a second is exactly how they end up understanding things faster.

they say less, better

they don't comment on everything. when they do speak, it's short and clear, and people remember it because it wasn't buried in a dozen other half thoughts.

they learn a little daily

they spend 5 minutes a day learning something outside their world: art, history, how the body works. a little every day quietly builds the range that looks effortless.
slides.texte_sophia:
they learn a little daily

i spend 5 minutes a day learning something outside my world: art, history, the body. i do it with the Sophia app, one lesson a day, and the range it gives you looks effortless.

slides.texte_overlay:
they change their mind

they say you're right, i hadn't thought of that, without any drama. changing your mind in public is a sign of a strong mind, not a weak one, and people trust it.

they read before bed

they read a few real pages before sleep instead of scrolling. the last thing you feed your brain at night is what it works on while you sleep, so they feed it something good.
